item.title: Oh Se-hoon: "In the final stages of the election, Jang Dong-hyuk showed up in Seoul... I had to put in some effort to avoid him." (오세훈 “선거 막판 장동혁 서울 출몰…그거 피하느라 신경 좀 썼다”)
item.description:
Oh Se-hoon, the Mayor of Seoul who secured a fifth term with a victory in the June 3 local elections, said, "There were difficult moments during the (campaign period) when I had to avoid Chairman Jang Dong-hyuk." (6·3 지방선거 승리로 5선 고지에 오른 오세훈 서울시장이 “(유세 기간) 장동혁 대표를 피하느라고 어려운 순간도 있었다”고 말했다.)

The Mayor responded to this on the TV Chosun program "Strong Rivals" on the 20th, when asked, "Among the various factors for your victory, there’s an analysis that the absence of a campaign support visit by Jang Dong-hyuk, the chair of the People Power Party, was key. Do you agree?" (오 시장은 20일 티브이(TV)조선 ‘강적들’에 출연해 ‘여러 승리 요인 가운데 장동혁 국민의힘 대표의 지원 유세가 없었던 점이 주효했다는 분석이 있는데 동의하느냐’는 질문에 이같이 답했다.)

Mayor Oh said, "At first, he seemed to know we weren’t welcoming, so he naturally only toured the provinces. But in the last few days of the election, he came up to the capital region," adding, "And then he started showing up in Seoul. I thought clashing with him (Chairman Jang) wouldn’t help with votes, so I began avoiding him." He continued, "In the final day or two (of the election), the party started scheduling events overlapping with mine, so the staff handling my schedule had a tough time avoiding him and had to put in some effort." (오 시장은 “처음에는 우리가 달가워하지 않는다는 걸 알아서 그런지 (장 대표가) 당연히 지방만 돌았는데 선거 마지막 며칠을 남겨놓고는 수도권으로 올라왔다”며 “그러면서 서울에 출몰하기 시작했는데 정말 (장 대표와) 부딪히는 것은 득표에 도움이 안 된다고 생각했기 때문에 피하기 시작했다”고 말했다. 이어 “(선거) 마지막 하루이틀 남겨놓고는 (장 대표와) 내 동선하고 겹치는 일정이 당에서 나오기 시작해서 일정 짜는 친구들이 그거 피해 다니느라고 신경 좀 썼다”고 덧붙였다.)

Regarding the mounting calls within the party for Chairman Jang to step down, Oh said, "Given the tendencies of our party’s National Assembly members, they wouldn’t want a resignation that looks like he’s being chased out in an undignified manner—if only for their own pride," adding, "I think it will take a bit more time (for the resignation)." Earlier, on the 17th, Mayor Oh had stated, "The Jang Dong-hyuk leadership has reached the end of its life." (당에서 장 대표 사퇴 요구가 빗발치는 상황에 대해선 “우리 당 국회의원님들의 성향상 볼썽사납게 쫓겨나는 듯한 모습의 퇴진은 원치 않을 것이다. 본인들의 자존심을 위해서라도”라며 “아마 (사퇴에는) 시간이 좀 더 소요될 것이라고 생각한다”고 말했다. 앞서 오 시장은 지난 17일 “장동혁 지도부는 수명을 다했다”고 말한 바 있다.)

On Na Kyung-won, a People Power Party lawmaker, who said on the 12th, "If I were the (Oh Se-hoon) Seoul Mayor elect, I would have declared a by-election," Oh responded, "I don’t interpret that as an ‘anti’ against me. I see it as a reply directed at the young Seoul citizens at Olympic Park." He added, "On the day she said that, we happened to have a meal together, and she even brought a congratulatory cake." (나경원 국민의힘 의원이 지난 12일 “내가 (오세훈) 서울시장 당선자였다면 재선거를 선언했을 것”이라고 말한 데 대해선 “나에 대한 ‘안티’로 해석하지 않고 올림픽공원에 있는 젊은 서울 시민들에 대한 화답 차원의 말로 생각한다”고 말했다. 그러면서 “그렇게 이야기한 날 마침 식사를 같이했는데 축하 케이크도 사 왔다”고 덧붙였다.)

Meanwhile, Mayor Oh revealed that he has contacted the presidential office, requesting a meeting before a cabinet meeting, and is awaiting a response. Oh said, "If I could have just 30 minutes (to talk to President Lee Jae-myung), I’ve asked for an opportunity to explain the issues I see in the housing market, rather than debating during the cabinet meeting," adding, "He said he’d think about it after returning from abroad and get back to me. Now that he’s back, I’m waiting." (한편, 오 시장은 국무회의 전에 자신을 불러달라고 대통령실에 연락하고 답을 기다리고 있다고 밝혔다. 오 시장은 “30분 정도만 (이재명 대통령에게) 이야기할 기회를 주면 굳이 국무회의 들어가서 따지는 게 아니라 내가 생각하는 주택시장의 문제점을 말씀드릴 기회를 달라고 요청을 했다”며 “(이 대통령) 귀국 뒤에 생각해서 연락을 주겠다고 했는데 이제 귀국했으니 기다리고 있다”고 말했다.)

Lee Yu-jin, reporter yjlee@hani.co.kr (이유진 기자 yjlee@hani.co.kr)

item.title: Woo Won-shik: “What Remains If the Party Convention Is Held with Mockery and Division?”…Declares Non-Candidacy (우원식 “조롱과 분열로 전당대회 치르면 뭐가 남나”…불출마 선언)
item.description:
Former National Assembly Speaker Woo Won-shik has declared he will not run in the Democratic Party of Korea’s party convention scheduled for August. Criticizing the internal conflicts that have emerged during the leadership race, former Speaker Woo stated, “The Democratic Party must first clarify who it is a party for and what this convention is intended to achieve. Only then can the competition for party leadership have meaning.” (우원식 전 국회의장이 오는 8월 치러지는 더불어민주당 전당대회 불출마를 선언했다. 우 전 의장은 당권 경쟁 과정에서 불거진 당내 갈등을 비판하며 “민주당이 누구를 위한 정당인지, 이번 전당대회가 무엇을 위한 전당대회인지부터 분명히 해야 한다”며 “그래야 당권 경쟁도 의미를 가질 수 있다”고 말했다.)

On the 21st, former Speaker Woo posted on Facebook a message titled ‘Statement by Rep. Woo Won-shik Regarding the Democratic Party Convention,’ saying, “I have no intention to run in this convention. Who is the Democratic Party for? What is this convention for?” (우 전 의장은 21일 페이스북에 ‘민주당 전당대회 관련 우원식 의원 입장문’이라는 글을 올려 저는 이번 전당대회에 나갈 생각이 없다”며 “누구를 위한 민주당인가. 무엇을 위한 전당대회인가”라고 했다.)

Former Speaker Woo remarked, “Derogatory terms that are hard to put into words are being mobilized to attack internal opponents. It is embarrassing and shameful. If we hold a convention causing mutual wounds, ridiculing each other, finding faults, and fostering division, what will be left of our party afterward?” (우 전 의장은 “차마 입에 담기 어려운 멸칭들이 내부의 상대를 공격하기 위해 동원되고 있다. 민망하고 부끄럽다”며 “이렇게 서로에게 상처를 내고, 상대를 조롱하고, 흠집을 잡고, 분열을 키우면서 전당대회를 치르고 나면, 그다음에 우리 당에는 무엇이 남는 것인가”라고 했다.)

He continued, “If we fail to properly heed the warning from the people in the last local elections, there is no future for the Democratic Party. In particular, I urge those seeking to run in the convention to be as courageous and honest as possible, looking squarely at the reality our party faces.” (이어 그는 “지난 지방선거에서 국민께 받은 경고, 그 뜻을 제대로 새기지 못하면 (민주당에) 미래는 없다”며 “특히 전당대회에 나서려는 분들은 최대한 용기 있고, 정직하게 우리 민주당이 직면한 현실을 있는 그대로 봐줄 것을 요청한다”고 했다.)

Former Speaker Woo said, “When the Democratic Party splits internally and draws swords against each other, it invariably shrinks and faces defeat. We endured the pain of the previous administration, yet in just a year, at a time when we should be expanding the path of democratic governance further, we saw division in Pyeongtaek during the local elections, and internal conflicts have become so severe that it’s hard to see ahead.” (우 전 의장은 “민주당은 내부에서 갈라지고 서로를 향해 칼을 겨누었을 때, 어김없이 쪼그라들고 패배했다”며 “지난 정권 그 고통을 겪고 단 1년, 민주정부의 길을 더 확장해도 모자랄 판에 지방선거 때 평택에서 분열하고, 내부도 앞을 내다보기 어려워질 정도로 갈등이 심하다”고 했다.)

Former Speaker Woo added, “As a lifelong member of the Democratic Party who has walked alongside the marginalized in the field, I offer this plea because I can no longer bear to watch the party’s division and antagonism. Let’s first clarify who the Democratic Party is for and what this convention is for. Only then will the leadership race have meaning.” (우 전 의장은 “평생을 민주당의 당인으로, 현장에서 을과 함께 걸어온 사람으로서 당의 분열과 반목을 차마 더는 지켜보기가 힘들어서 드리는 당부”라며 “민주당이 누구를 위한 정당인지, 이 전당대회가 무엇을 위한 전당대회인지부터 분명히 하자. 그래야 당권경쟁도 의미가 있다”고 했다.)

Former Speaker Woo, a five-term veteran lawmaker, returned to the Democratic Party after completing his term as the Speaker of the first half of the 22nd National Assembly on the 29th of last month. (5선 중진인 우 전 의장은 지난달 29일 22대 국회 전반기 의장 임기를 마친 뒤 다시 민주당으로 복귀했다.)

item.title: Jung Cheong-rae: "A Flower That Blooms Without Swaying..." Visits South Jeolla, Citing Do Jong-hwan's Poem Again (정청래 “흔들리지 않고 피는 꽃…” 전남 찾아 도종환 시 또 언급)
item.description:
Jung Cheong-rae, leader of the Democratic Party of Korea, visited Mihwangsa Temple in Haenam County, South Jeolla Province on the 20th, once again referencing poet Do Jong-hwan's "A Flower That Blooms While Swaying," saying, "Whenever you face difficult or hard times, I hope you think of this poem and take heart." Jung also emphasized his connection to the temple, saying, "I've always stopped by Mihwangsa on my way to my in-laws' house once a year." <<> Meanwhile, as Jung visited Honam region successively—including South Jeolla on the 20th after North Jeolla on the 19th—and repeatedly quoted the poem, there are interpretations both inside and outside the party that this reflects his discomfort amid pressure not to run in the upcoming party convention. Within and outside the party, following the results of local elections, a negative sentiment has formed around Jung's bid for a second term as party leader at the August convention, particularly among those not aligned with the party's power base. <<> Ha Eo-young Reporter haha@hani.co.kr (정청래 더불어민주당 대표가 지난 20일 전남 해남군 미황사를 방문해 “힘들 때마다 어려울 때마다 이 시를 생각하면서 힘내시기 바란다”며 도종환 시인의 ‘흔들리며 피는 꽃’을 거듭 언급했다. 정 대표는 앞서 18일 이재명 대통령을 성남 서울공항에서 마중한 뒤 시 구절을 인용해 “다 흔들리면서 젖으면서 가는 게 인생 아니겠나”라고 말한 바 있다.)

item.title: Kim Min-seok Holds Reform Forum on Election Commission, Says “We Need a One-Point Constitutional Amendment” (김민석, 선관위 개혁 토론회 열어 “원 포인트 개헌 해야”)
item.description:
Prime Minister Kim Min-seok stated on the 21st, “Even through constitutional amendment, the only answer is to respect the independence of the National Election Commission while subjecting it to external checks and oversight. I’ve been deeply considering the so-called ‘one-point constitutional amendment’ these days.” (김민석 국무총리가 21일 “개헌을 통해서라도 선관위의 독립성은 존중하되 외부의 견제와 감시를 받게 하는 쪽으로 가는 것만이 답이 아닌가. 요새 이른바 ‘원포인트 개헌’이라는 문제를 깊이 생각해보고 있다”라고 말했다.)

In a citizen forum on reforming the National Election Commission held that morning at Korea National Sport University in Songpa-gu, Seoul, Prime Minister Kim said, “As it happens, President (Lee) also mentioned that,” referring to President Lee Jae-myung’s earlier remarks. On the 19th, President Lee held a briefing at the Cheongwadae Spring and Autumn Hall on the outcomes of his European tour and participation in the G7 summit, stating, “We have no authority to control, monitor, or check them, and we don’t even have formal appointment or dismissal power over the Election Commission chairperson. They elect their own members in rotation among themselves. If the ruling and opposition parties agree, shouldn’t we consider a ‘one-point constitutional amendment’ to allow oversight of the Election Commission?” (김 총리는 이날 오전 서울 송파구 한국체육대학교에서 열린 선거관리위원회 개혁 관련 시민 토론회에서 “마침 (이) 대통령도 그 말을 했다”며 이같이 말했다. 이재명 대통령은 지난 19일 청와대 춘추관에서 유럽 순방과 주요 7개국 정상회의(G7) 참석 결과 브리핑을 열어 “우리에겐 통제·감시·견제 권한이 없고 하다못해 선관위원장에 대한 형식적인 임면권조차도 없다. 스스로 자기들끼리 돌아가면서 뽑게 돼 있다”며 “여야 간 의견이 일치된다면, 선관위에 대해 (감시할 수 있는) ‘원포인트 개헌’이라도 해야 하지 않을까”라고 했다.)

Kim further said, “I’ve been recently asking constitutional scholars for their opinions, and I’m hearing suggestions from them on how to go about a one-point constitutional amendment regarding issues like the composition of the Election Commission and its independence. If possible, I hope we can pursue this through public discourse that transcends the ruling and opposition parties.” (김 총리는 “제가 최근에 헌법학자들에게도 자꾸 의견을 여쭤보는데, 선관위 구성의 문제, 독립성의 문제 등등에 대해 원포인트 개헌을 이렇게 하자, 저렇게 하자는 말씀 주는 걸 듣고 있다”며 “할 수 있다면 여와 야를 넘어서 국민적 공론화를 통해 이걸 추진해보면 좋겠다”고 말했다.)

The forum that day was attended by six participants from youth, academic, and civil society circles, including Kim Tae-yoon, former and current president of the National Student Council Union; Jang Young-soo, professor emeritus at Korea University Law School; and Lee So-young, executive committee member of the People’s Solidarity for Participatory Democracy’s Parliamentary Monitoring Center. (이날 토론회에는 김태윤 전·현직 총학생회 연합 대표, 장영수 고려대 법학전문대학원 명예교수, 이소영 참여연대 의정감시센터 실행위원 등 청년과 학계, 시민사회계 인사 6명이 참석했다.)

After the panel discussion, Kim remarked, “I’ll be stepping down from the prime minister’s post soon, and as that time approaches, valuable insights like these are sinking in more deeply. I’ve come to think that a comprehensive discussion or public debate on the overall election system is inevitable.” (패널 토론이 끝난 뒤 김 총리는 “제가 이제 조만간 총리직을 내려놓는데, 그때가 되니 귀한 말씀들이 이렇게 더 쏙쏙 들어온다”며 “선거 제도 전반에 대한 포괄적인 토론 내지 공론화가 불가피하겠구나 생각하게 됐다”고 말했다.)

Kim added, “There’s talk about early voting, voting hours, and a variety of technical issues. Even if we can’t resolve everything this time, I think we need to start the discussion. I’m considering whether the government could find ways to support public discourse led by young people and university students.” (김 총리는 “사전 투표 얘기도 나오고 투표 시간 얘기도 나오고 막 다양한 기술적인 문제까지 나오지 않나. 이번에 다 해결은 안 돼도 토론은 시작해야겠다는 생각을 하게 됐다”며 “청년, 대학생들이 주도하는 공론화를 정부가 지원하는 방법을 좀 찾아볼 수 있지 않을까 생각한다”고 말했다.)

Reporter Goh Kyung-joo goh@hani.co.kr (고경주 기자 goh@hani.co.kr)

item.title: President Lee Appoints Nam Jae-heon, Head of Arctic Route Promotion Headquarters, as New Vice Minister of Oceans and Fisheries (이 대통령, 신임 해수부 차관에 남재헌 북극항로추진본부장 임명)
item.description:
President Lee Jae-myung appointed Nam Jae-heon, head of the Arctic Route Promotion Headquarters at the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF), as the new Vice Minister of Oceans and Fisheries on the 21st. (이재명 대통령이 21일 신임 해양수산부 차관에 남재헌 해수부 북극항로추진본부장을 임명했다.)

Kang Yu-jeong, Senior Presidential Spokesperson for Cheong Wa Dae, announced this in a written briefing the same day, stating, "Vice Minister Nam is a representative port expert who has served as Director of the Ports Bureau at MOF and Head of the Busan North Port Integrated Development Promotion Team, and is a veteran bureaucrat with strong execution skills and outstanding problem-solving abilities." (강유정 청와대 수석대변인은 이날 서면 브리핑을 통해 이같이 밝히며 “남 차관은 해수부 항만국장과 부산항북항통합개발추진단장을 역임한 대표적인 항만 전문가로 업무 추진력을 두루 갖추고, 문제 해결 능력이 뛰어난 정통 관료”라고 말했다.)

Senior Spokesperson Kang added, "Vice Minister Nam served as the inaugural head of the Arctic Route Promotion Headquarters, where he is recognized for laying a solid foundation for pioneering the Arctic route, including the enactment of the Special Act on Arctic Routes, and creating the maritime capital region," and said, "He is the right person to lead the era of the Arctic route based on his expertise in oceans and fisheries and to build a global maritime powerhouse through the completion of the maritime capital." (강 수석대변인은 이어 “남 차관은 초대 북극항로추진본부 본부장을 맡아 북극항로특별법 제정 등 북극항로 개척과 해양수도권 조성을 위한 기반을 착실히 마련한 것으로 평가받고 있다”며 “해양수산에 대한 전문성을 바탕으로 북극항로 시대를 주도하고, 해양수도 완성을 통해 글로벌 해양강국을 건설해 나갈 적임자”라고 말했다.)

Meanwhile, former Vice Minister of Oceans and Fisheries Kim Seong-beom was elected in the June 3 by-election for a member of the National Assembly in Seogwipo, Jeju Island. (앞서 김성범 전 해수부 차관은 지난 6·3 지방선거 국회의원 보궐선거 때 제주 서귀포에 출마해 당선됐다.)

item.title: Shin Jang-sik proposes to Democratic Party: "Let's form a one-team platform... must complete prosecution reform before Constitution Day" (신장식, 민주 향해 “원팀 플랫폼 구성하자…검찰개혁 제헌절 전에 끝내야”)
item.description:
Shin Jang-sik, Acting Leader of the Fatherland Innovation Party, proposed on the 21st to the Democratic Party, "Let's form a 'government operation one-team platform' so that the entire democratic reform and progressive camp can unite as one and pool all capabilities." (신장식 조국혁신당 대표 권한대행이 21일 민주당을 향해 “민주개혁 진보 진영 전체가 하나가 되어 모든 역량을 총결집할 수 있도록 ‘국정운영 원팀 플랫폼’을 구성하자”고 제안했다.)

At a press briefing at the National Assembly that day, Acting Leader Shin said, "What we need now is the power of a grand alliance. It is time for all of us to become a 'one team' with strong teamwork for the success of the people's sovereign government." He added, "If we upgrade the roundtable discussions from the last presidential election into a standing national affairs consultative body, the engine of state affairs operation will run even hotter." <<> When asked if the one-team platform is related to a merger, he replied, "I don't think the merger itself is the goal. The Innovation Party considers self-reliance as foundational, solidarity as essential, and merger as optional." He continued, "The failure of solidarity led to disappointing results in this local election. When I think about 2028 (general election) and 2030 (presidential election), it even sends a chill down my spine," adding, "Regarding how the democratic reform and progressive forces unite, the methodology is something we will need to debate later." <<> Acting Leader Shin emphasized the need to expedite prosecution reforms, including the supplementary investigation powers of the prosecution. He stated, "Prosecution reform must be completed before Constitution Day," and noted, "There are talks that the Democratic Party might postpone prosecution reform until after its party convention. That is the scenario that those opposing prosecution reform hope for." He also argued, "Since the President has delegated discussions on supplementary investigation powers to the National Assembly, there is no reason for the Assembly to wait for the multiple proposals from the Prime Minister's Office's prosecution reform task force. There is no need to wait for the formation of the Assembly's standing committees either." <<> Acting Leader Shin said, "As soon as the Innovation Party's party convention ends in July, we will embark on full-scale livelihood reforms. The Fatherland Innovation Party proposes that the National Assembly move forward with tax system adjustments on real estate unearned income and the reintroduction of the financial investment income tax." He also stated, "Let the National Assembly take the lead in establishing special measures to resolve the jeonse (housing deposit) crisis and devising plans to invest the tax revenue secured from the semiconductor boom into people's lives to address inequality and polarization." <<> By Ha Eo-young, Reporter haha@hani.co.kr (신 권한대행은 이날 국회 기자간담회에서 “지금 우리에게 필요한 것은 거대한 연합의 힘이다. 우리 모두가 국민주권정부의 성공을 위해 끈끈한 팀워크를 가진 ‘원팀’이 되어야 할 때”라며 이렇게 말했다. 그는 “지난 대선 당시의 원탁회의를 국정상설협의체로 격상한다면, 국정운영의 엔진은 훨씬 더 뜨겁게 가동될 것”이라고 말했다.)

item.title: People Power Party Summons Election from 8 Years Ago, Claims "Number of Elected Officials Increased…Jang Dong-hyeok's Achievement" in Mental Victory (국힘, 8년 전 선거 소환해 “당선인 늘어…장동혁 성과” 정신승리)
item.description:
The People Power Party compared the results of the June 3 local elections to those from eight years ago, rather than four years ago, praising themselves on the 21st by saying, "The number of elected candidates has increased, and Party Leader Jang Dong-hyeok made dedicated efforts." This is interpreted as the Jang Dong-hyeok leadership refuting the 'responsibility for the local election defeat' narrative and making clear that there is no intention to step down from the party leader position. (국민의힘이 6·3 지방선거 결과를 4년 전이 아닌 8년 전 지방선거와 견주며 “당선인 수가 늘었고 장동혁 대표도 헌신적인 노력을 했다”고 21일 자화자찬했다. 장동혁 지도부가 ‘지방선거 패배 책임론’을 반박하며 대표직에서 물러날 뜻이 없음을 분명히 한 것으로 해석된다.)

The People Power Party released a press release on that day titled 'Analysis of the June 3 Local and National Assembly By-elections Results,' stating, "In this election, we produced 4 metropolitan government heads and 95 basic government heads," and claimed, "Compared to the 2018 local elections, which were held immediately after becoming the opposition party under the same circumstances, the number of elected officials increased by 2 and 42, respectively." Despite the number of elected metropolitan government heads in this local election falling to just 4, a significant decrease from the 2022 local elections (12), they highlighted it as an achievement by comparing it to the disastrous 2018 local elections instead of the 2022 ones. There was no mention or analysis of the defeat. (국민의힘은 이날 ‘6·3 지방선거 및 국회의원 재·보궐선거 결과 분석’이라는 보도자료를 내고 “이번 선거에서 광역단체장 4명, 기초단체장 95명 등을 배출했다”며 “동일하게 야당이 된 직후 치른 2018년 지방선거와 비교하면 당선인 수가 각각 2명·42명 증가했다”고 밝혔다. 이번 지방선거에서 광역단체장 당선자수가 4명에 그치며 2022년 지방선거(12명)보다 때보다 크게 줄어들었음에도 2022년 지방선거 대신 참패했던 2018년 지방선거와 견주며 성과를 강조한 것이다. 패배에 대한 언급이나 분석은 없었다.)

In this document, the People Power Party highlighted the activities of Leader Jang. The document praised Jang, stating, "Leader Jang covered all 16 cities and provinces, giving his all for the election of candidates," and "Since taking office, Leader Jang has revised the party constitution and rules to establish a fair nomination system and has innovated the nomination process and overall organizational operations." (국민의힘은 이 자료에서 장 대표의 활동을 부각했다. 자료는 “장 대표는 16개 시·도 전체를 아우르며 후보자들의 당선을 위해 혼신을 다했다”, “장 대표 취임 이후 공정한 공천 시스템을 구축하기 위해 당헌·당규를 정비하고, 공천 절차와 조직 운영 전반을 혁신해왔다”고 장 대표를 추어올렸다.)

The People Power Party's release of a self-serving election evaluation document appears to strongly reflect Leader Jang's determination not to resign from his post. A party official said, "Without reviewing the election results, there is talk of Leader Jang resigning, and we compiled this to allow discussions based on facts." In response, a three-term lawmaker pointed out, "Comparing to the elections from eight years ago, not four, is inappropriate," and added, "It's problematic that the document fails to mention that areas where we saw achievements conducted their campaigns excluding Leader Jang." (국민의힘이 아전인수격의 선거 평가 자료를 낸 것은 대표직에서 사퇴하지 않겠다는 장 대표의 의지가 강하게 반영된 것으로 보인다. 국민의힘 관계자는 “선거 결과를 복기하지 않은 채 장 대표 사퇴론 얘기가 나오고 있는데, 사실관계를 기반으로 얘기할 수 있도록 정리한 것”이라고 말했다. 이에 대해 한 3선 의원은 “4년 전이 아니라 8년 전 선거와 비교하는 것은 맞지 않는다”며 “이번 선거에서 성과를 낸 곳도 장 대표를 배제하고 선거운동을 했다는 점을 밝히지 않은 것은 문제가 있다”고 지적했다.)

The document was not even reported in advance to Floor Leader Jeong Jeom-sik. Appearing on MBN News that afternoon, Floor Leader Jeong stated, "I was not briefed on (the document) in advance," and added, "The comparison to 2018 is an analysis at the party secretariat level that did not sufficiently reflect the opinions of lawmakers." (해당 자료는 정점식 원내대표에게도 사전에 보고 되지 않았다. 정 원내대표는 이날 오후 엠비엔(MBN) 뉴스에 출연해 “(자료를) 사전에 보고받지 못했다”며 “(2018년과 비교한 것은) 의원들 의견이 충분히 반영되지 않은 당 사무처 차원의 분석”이라고 말했다.)

Leader Jang ceased public activities after the last election review general meeting of lawmakers on the 17th and has been hospitalized in a Seoul hospital since the 18th, citing health issues. Amidst speculation within the party that Jang might reshuffle party leadership to quell internal discontent, rumors are circulating that pro-power lawmaker Park Su-yeong will take on the role of policy committee chairman. (장 대표는 지난 17일 선거소청 의원총회를 마지막으로 공개활동을 중단하고 18일부터 건강상의 문제라며 서울 시내 병원에 입원한 상태다. 당내에서는 장 대표가 당내 불만을 잠재우려 당직 개편을 할 수 있다는 전망이 나오는 가운데 당권파인 박수영 의원이 정책위의장을 맡을 것이라는 말이 돈다.)

item.title: “Mr. President, I Suggest a 10-Minute Break”…What’s Happening in the State Council Members’ Group Chat? (“대통령님, 10분만 휴식 건의합니다”…국무위원 단톡방에 무슨 일?)
item.description:
“Mr. President. I suggest a 10-minute break after two hours.” (“대통령님. 2시간 지나면 10분 휴식 건의합니다.”)

According to a ruling party source on the 21st, a state council member recently posted a message in a Telegram group chat with President Lee Jae-myung, requesting a break if the cabinet meeting runs long. The gist was, “Elderly state council members might find it difficult, so please give us 10 minutes to rest.” In response, President Lee instructed the head of the Office for Government Policy Coordination, “Give me a signal after two hours,” and added a follow-up message: “I’ll try to wrap up the cabinet meeting within two hours if possible.” Several state council members then reportedly ‘hearted’ the president’s message (indicating a ‘like’). (21일 여권 관계자의 말을 들어보면, 최근 한 국무위원이 이재명 대통령과 같이 있는 텔레그램 단체방에 국무회의가 길어지면 휴식을 달라고 요청하는 글을 올렸다고 한다. “연로하신 국무위원들이 힘들 수 있으니 10분 쉬는 시간을 달라”는 취지였다. 그러자 이 대통령은 국무조정실장에게 “2시간이 지나면 사인을 달라”고 지시했고, 재차 “가능하면 2시간 안에 국무회의를 마치도록 하겠다”는 메시지를 올렸다. 그러자 여러 명의 국무위원들이 이 대통령의 글에 (‘좋아요’를 뜻하는) ‘하트’를 눌렀다고 한다.)

The suggestion for a break among state council members arose because the weekly Tuesday ‘live-broadcasted cabinet meetings’ regularly exceed two hours. It’s said that many council members even avoid drinking water properly to prevent needing bathroom breaks. On May 20, the cabinet meeting lasted about 4 hours and 30 minutes without any break, and the meeting on the 2nd, just before President Lee’s European tour, went on for nearly three hours as well. (국무위원들 사이에 ‘휴식 건의’가 나온 것은 매주 화요일 진행되는 ‘생중계 국무회의’가 기본 2시간을 넘어가기 때문이다. 화장실을 가지 않기 위해 물도 제대로 마시지 않는 국무위원들도 적지 않다고 한다. 지난 5월 20일 국무회의는 4시간 30분가량 쉬는 시간 없이 진행됐고, 이 대통령의 유럽 순방 직전인 지난 2일 회의도 3시간 가까이 이어졌다.)

The ‘live-broadcasted cabinet meeting’ is now one of the iconic scenes of the Lee Jae-myung administration. However, state council members remain on high alert, not knowing when the president might spring a surprise question, and their every facial expression is captured by cameras. Additionally, if they haven’t properly grasped the issues at hand, their lack of preparation is broadcast nationwide, prompting some council members to go so far as to assign dedicated staff specifically to monitor relevant matters, putting significant effort into preparation. (현재 ‘생중계 국무회의’는 이재명 정부를 상징하는 장면 가운데 하나다. 하지만 국무위원들은 대통령이 언제 ‘기습 질문’을 할지 모르는 데다 작은 표정까지 카메라에 잡혀 초긴장 상태다. 또 현안을 제대로 파악하지 않고 있으면 그 모습이 전국에 생중계되기 때문에 일부 국무위원들은 관련 현안을 챙기는 전담 인력까지 따로 둘 정도로 준비에 공을 들이고 있다고 한다.)

A ruling party source said, “Because the president meticulously understands every issue, state council members are under immense tension.” They added, “Since work orders can come through the Telegram chat at any time, they’re effectively on standby 24 hours a day.” (여권 관계자는 “대통령이 꼼꼼하게 현안을 다 파악하기 때문에 국무위원들이 긴장 상태가 높다”며 “텔레그램 방의 업무지시도 언제 올지 모르기 때문에 24시간 대기 상태라고 보면 된다”고 말했다.)

By Seo Young-ji, Reporter yj@hani.co.kr (서영지 기자 yj@hani.co.kr)

item.title: South Korea and U.S. Discuss North Korea’s Nuclear Program...Trump Turns Attention to U.S.-North Korea Dialogue (북핵 대화 나눈 한미....트럼프, 북-미 대화로 눈길 돌리나)
item.description:
As President Lee Jae-myung revealed the conversation he had with U.S. President Donald Trump during the official dinner of the Group of Seven (G7) summit regarding North Korea’s nuclear issue, attention is now focused on the possibility of future U.S.-North Korea talks. <<> In a press conference held at the presidential office on the 19th, President Lee stated, “President Trump mentioned that he himself posted a photo on social media of him walking in the garden with Chairman Kim Jong Un (on the 13th), and said, ‘It’s time to pay attention to the North Korean issue.’” President Lee added that President Trump “had the idea that he should engage in dialogue with North Korean State Affairs Commission Chairman Kim Jong Un.” This highlights that as the war between the U.S. and Israel-Iran subsides, Trump is shifting his focus to dialogue with North Korea. <<> President Lee also shared his advice to Trump on resolving the North Korean nuclear issue: “I told him that now is not the right time to approach the North Korean nuclear issue the way we deal with other countries.” He explained, “I outlined a phased approach—first, stop additional production of nuclear materials in the short term, then move toward reduction once stable, and finally, when trust is built and security guarantees are in place, advance toward denuclearization.” Lee Woo-tae, a senior research fellow at the Korea Institute for National Unification, told The Hankyoreh on the 21st, “In an environment where it’s difficult to completely win the war with Iran, President Trump needs a diplomatic achievement through dialogue with Chairman Kim Jong Un. The conditions have been set for the U.S. to focus on a ‘deal’ with North Korea.” <<> Views on the possibility of U.S.-North Korea talks are mixed. With North Korea insisting on recognition of its status as a nuclear state, simply proposing negotiation agendas like disarmament aimed at denuclearization is an obstacle. Kim Yo Jong, vice department director of the North Korean Workers’ Party, firmly stated on the 18th that denuclearization is an “irreversible line.” Moon Seong-mook, director of the Unification Strategy Center at the Korea National Strategy Institute, said, “If U.S.-North Korea talks proceed, we should consider the possibility of negotiating nuclear disarmament while treating North Korea’s nuclear status as a fait accompli.” <<> Given that North Korea has defined inter-Korean relations as “hostile two-state relations,” even if U.S.-North Korea talks are held, it remains uncertain whether this will lead to an improvement in inter-Korean relations. President Lee stated, “It’s difficult for the Republic of Korea to open a path to peaceful coexistence on its own,” adding, “We must strive to create conditions so that dialogue can center around the U.S.” Choi Yong-hwan, vice president of the Institute for National Security Strategy, said, “Amid global arms race, discussing arms control on the Korean Peninsula is challenging,” and added, “Chairman Kim would meet with the U.S. as long as denuclearization isn’t mentioned. In that case, it would just stop at general discussions about North Korea’s nuclear program, and shifting the atmosphere on the Peninsula to discuss improving inter-Korean relations is a separate issue.” <<> However, there are expectations that Trump might set phased goals for talks with North Korea to achieve results. Min Jung-hoon, a professor at the Korea National Diplomatic Academy, said, “The first Trump administration (which held U.S.-North Korea talks in 2018-2019) aimed for a comprehensive deal with a ‘big deal or no deal’ strategy on the nuclear issue. Now, the stance is that something is better than nothing.” He added, “Rather than setting a final goal for the talks, a phased, give-and-take approach could be effective.” <<> The role of China in facilitating U.S.-North Korea dialogue is also gaining traction. Vice President Choi Yong-hwan noted, “To sway North Korea, the opinions of China and Russia are crucial. Particularly, with the planned U.S.-China summit in September, the China APEC summit (in November), and the U.S. G20 summit (in December), when U.S. and Chinese leaders meet, opportunities for U.S.-North Korea talks should be created.” <<> Reporter Jang Ye-ji penj@hani.co.kr (이재명 대통령이 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령과 주요 7개국(G7) 정상회의 공식 만찬에서 북핵 문제를 두고 나눴던 대화를 공개하면서, 향후 북-미 회담 가능성에 관심이 쏠린다.)

item.title: [Exclusive] Noh Tae-ak came to work only once a month... and collected an allowance of 4.25 million won ([단독] 노태악, 한 달에 단 1번 출근한 뒤…425만원 수당 챙겨)
item.description:
Former National Election Commission (NEC) Chairman Noh Tae-ak was found to have received an allowance of 4.25 million won while coming to work only once a month. Even on the days he did come in, he often attended events unrelated to election management, such as New Year's concerts. <<> According to a document titled 'Attendance records and allowance payments for the NEC Chairman over the past three years,' submitted by Democratic Party of Korea lawmaker Yoon Geon-young to the NEC on the 21st, former Chairman Noh came to work for just one day in November 2024 for a regular meeting but received 4.25 million won in allowances. In July 2024, he came to work for a total of two days to attend a regular meeting and a Constitution Day event, and collected 3.5 million won. <<> Even on the days he was present, he often participated in events that appeared unrelated to actual election management duties. In January 2024, an election year, former Chairman Noh came to work six times in total. On three of those days, his schedule involved activities unrelated to election management, such as a New Year's social gathering, a New Year's concert, and the opening ceremony of the Winter Youth Olympics. The New Year's social gathering and concert were events he attended upon the invitation of former President Yoon Seok-yeol's five key officials (the National Assembly Speaker, Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, President of the Constitutional Court, Prime Minister, and NEC Chairman). Additionally, attending events like the Czech Independence Day celebration (October 27, 2025) and Sports Day (November 11, 2025) was also recorded as work attendance. <<> In the case of part-time NEC commissioners, there were instances where they received allowances exceeding 2 million won without coming to work for even a single day. According to data submitted by the NEC, one particular part-time NEC commissioner did not attend meetings in October and November last year, missing every day, yet still received 2.15 million won per month in allowances through items such as 'fair election promotion activity fees.' This is because more than half of their allowances come from these activity fees, which are paid regardless of attendance. The allowances for part-time commissioners consist of attendance pay, agenda review pay, and fair election promotion activity fees, with the latter being the largest component. For the NEC chairman, this amounts to 2.9 million won per month, and for commissioners, 2.15 million won per month. <<> Lawmaker Yoon stated, "Under the current system, where the chairman and commissioners receive fixed monthly allowances without playing any role related to the actual work of the NEC, even if it is a part-time system, it is difficult for the public to accept this as a matter of common sense." He added, "This issue warrants a thorough re-examination during the restructuring process of the NEC in the wake of this incident." <<> Reporter Ko Kyung-joo goh@hani.co.kr (노태악 전 중앙선거관리위원장이 한달에 하루만 출근하고도 425만원의 수당을 받은 적이 있는 것으로 나타났다. 출근한 날도 신년음악회 등 선거 관리 업무와 거리가 있는 일정에 참석한 경우가 다수 있었다.)

item.title: President Lee's Second-Year Blue House Reshuffle: Han Chan-sik as Senior Secretary for Civil Affairs, Kim Kyung-ja as Senior Secretary for Social Affairs (이 대통령 국정 2년차 청와대 개편…민정수석 한찬식·사회수석 김경자)
item.description:
On the 21st, President Lee Jae-myung appointed Sung Ki-hong, former CEO of Yonhap News Agency, as the new Senior Secretary for Public Relations and Communication at the Blue House, and Han Chan-sik, a lawyer at Kim & Chang Law Firm, as Senior Secretary for Civil Affairs. Kim Kyung-ja, a visiting professor at the College of General Education at Woosuk University and a former member of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU), was appointed as Senior Secretary for Social Affairs. This reshuffle of some senior secretary-level aides marks the start of the second year of his administration, aimed at accelerating the execution of key national agendas. <<> Kang Hoon-sik, Chief of Staff to the President, held a briefing at the Blue House's Chunchugwan that day, stating, "President Lee has newly appointed the Senior Secretary for Public Relations and Communication, the Senior Secretary for Civil Affairs, and the Senior Secretary for Social Affairs, as well as the First and Third Deputy Directors of the National Security Office." He added, "This personnel change focuses on swiftly realizing the second-year vision of an 'Irreplaceable Republic of Korea,' building on the achievements of the past year." Kang Geon-jak, a member of the Future National Defense Strategy Committee under the direct authority of the President, was appointed as the First Deputy Director of the National Security Office, a senior-level position. Song Ki-ho, the Economic Security Secretary at the Third Deputy Director's Office of the National Security Office, was named the Third Deputy Director. Sung, the new Senior Secretary for Public Relations, previously worked as the political bureau chief, editorial writer, and news director at Yonhap News TV, and served as CEO of both Yonhap News Agency and Yonhap News TV. Chief of Staff Kang remarked, "As a veteran journalist with 30 years of experience, he is expected to attentively listen to the voices of the people and faithfully support government communication so that the public can easily perceive the administration's responses and achievements." <<> Han Chan-sik, the Senior Secretary for Civil Affairs (a graduate of the Judicial Research and Training Institute, 21st class), served as the Director of the Human Rights Bureau at the Ministry of Justice, the Chief Prosecutor of the Seoul Eastern District Prosecutors' Office, and the Chief Prosecutor of the Suwon District Prosecutors' Office. He retired from the prosecution in July 2019. Chief of Staff Kang explained, "Senior Secretary Han will strengthen accountability in the public service during the second year and ensure the smooth completion of prosecution reforms, including the establishment of the Serious Crimes Investigation Office and the Public Prosecution Office." Regarding Kim Kyung-ja, the Senior Secretary for Social Affairs, who is a former senior deputy chairperson of the KCTU, Chief of Staff Kang said, "As a pharmacist-turned-healthcare expert, labor activist, and civil society activist, she is a leader who has driven change in our society." On the same day, President Lee appointed Nam Jae-heon, head of the Arctic Sea Route Promotion Headquarters at the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF), as the Vice Minister of MOF, filling the vacancy left by former Vice Minister Kim Sung-beom, who won the June 3 by-election for a National Assembly seat in Seogwipo, Jeju. <<> By Seo Young-ji, Reporter: yj@hani.co.kr (이재명 대통령이 21일 신임 청와대 홍보소통수석과 민정수석에 성기홍 전 연합뉴스 대표이사와 한찬식 김앤장법률사무소 변호사를 임명했다. 사회수석에는 민주노총 출신인 김경자 우석대 교양대학 객원교수가 임명됐다. 2년차를 맞아 수석비서관급 참모를 일부 교체해 핵심 국정 과제 실행에 속도를 내겠다는 취지다.)

item.title: Ruling on ‘Salmon Party’ Perjury… Democratic Party: “Reason Special Counsel Is Needed”, People Power Party: “False Propaganda Revealed” (‘연어 술파티’ 위증 판결…민주 “특검 필요한 이유”, 국힘 “거짓 선동 밝혀져”)
item.description:
On the 20th, the court sentenced Lee Hwa-young, former Vice Governor of Gyeonggi Province for peace, to four months in prison for perjury regarding his ‘salmon party’ testimony, while acquitting him of charges of conspiring with former Ssangbangwool Chairman Kim Seong-tae in ‘Lee Jae-myung piecemeal donations’ (violation of the Political Funds Act). This sparked a clash between the ruling and opposition parties. The People Power Party attacked, claiming it revealed “a build-up for the cancellation of the indictment to ‘clear Lee Jae-myung of guilt,’ false fabrication,” while the Democratic Party of Korea retorted, “Rather, it’s a ruling that explains the necessity of introducing a special counsel for manipulated indictments.” <<> Na Kyung-won, a lawmaker from the People Power Party, said on Facebook on the 21st, “The salmon party suspicions have ultimately been confirmed as false. Yet the Democratic Party pushed for the impeachment of prosecutors, a parliamentary investigation, and even a special counsel based on this,” adding, “It amounts to mobilizing the state system for a build-up to cancel the indictment to ‘clear Lee Jae-myung of guilt,’ false fabrication.” Jeong Jeom-sik, the People Power Party’s floor leader, posted on Facebook the previous day, “The key basis for the Democratic Party’s claim to cancel the indictment in President Lee’s North Korea remittance case has collapsed,” and “The history of the Democratic Party’s false propaganda should now include the ‘salmon party propaganda.’” <<> In contrast, Lee Ju-hee, the Democratic Party’s deputy floor spokesperson, said in a written briefing, “The fact that 3 out of 7 jurors were not convinced of guilt in the ‘salmon party’ perjury charge means it did not meet the standard of ‘proof beyond a reasonable doubt’ required for a conviction under criminal procedure law,” arguing, “It should have been acquitted.” Members of the Democratic Party’s special committee for a parliamentary investigation into manipulated indictments also emphasized the acquittal of the former vice governor on the piecemeal donation conspiracy charges at a National Assembly press conference, stating, “By declaring the prosecution’s abuse of indictment rights, the court has made it clear that Yoon Seok-youl’s political prosecution engaged in ‘manipulated indictments to kill political opponents,’” stressing the need for introducing a special counsel. However, one Democratic Party lawmaker told The Hankyoreh, “The guilty verdict on the ‘salmon party’ testimony has somewhat weakened the momentum for pushing the manipulated indictment special counsel law.” <<> The previous day, the Suwon District Court sentenced the former vice governor to four months in prison for violating the Act on Testimony and Appraisal before the National Assembly in his first trial, acquitted him of violating the Political Funds Act, and dismissed charges of abuse of authority to obstruct rights, obstruction of official duties through fraudulent means, and violation of the Local Finance Act. <<> Kim Chae-un, Reporter cwk@hani.co.kr Jang Na-rae, Reporter wing@hani.co.kr (법원이 지난 20일 이화영 전 경기도 평화부지사의 ‘연어 술파티’ 증언이 허위라며 징역 4개월의 유죄를 선고하고, 김성태 전 쌍방울 회장과의 ‘이재명 쪼개기 후원 공모’(정치자금법 위반) 혐의에는 무죄를 선고한 것을 두고 여야가 공방을 벌였다. 국민의힘은 “‘이재명 죄 지우기’ 공소 취소를 위한 빌드업, 허위 날조”가 드러났다며 공격했고, 더불어민주당은 “오히려 조작기소 특검 도입의 필요성을 설명해주는 판결”이라며 맞받았다.)

item.title: Jung Cheong-rae vs. Kim Min-seok: ‘Power Struggle’ Ahead of National Convention… “Party-Government-Cheong Wa Dae as One Team” vs. “Disappointing Election Results” (정청래-김민석, 전대 앞 ‘기싸움’…“당·정·청 원팀” “선거 아쉬운 결과”)
item.description:
The race for the next party leader of the Democratic Party of Korea, to be elected at the August 17 National Convention, is heating up. As Representative Jung Cheong-rae is set to decide whether to seek a second term around the 24th, Prime Minister Kim Min-seok has entered the ‘final countdown’ to return to the National Assembly. Lawmaker Song Young-gil has also made remarks hinting at a possible candidacy. (더불어민주당 차기 당대표를 선출하는 8·17 전당대회 당권 경쟁이 본격화하고 있다. 정청래 대표가 오는 24일을 전후해 연임 도전 여부 결단을 내릴 예정인 가운데, 김민석 국무총리는 국회 복귀 ‘초읽기’에 들어갔다. 송영길 의원도 출마에 무게를 둔 발언을 내놓고 있다.)

On the afternoon of the 21st, Representative Jung and Prime Minister Kim attended the ‘June 3 Local Elections Winners’ Workshop’ held at the National Assembly Members’ Office Building in Yeouido, Seoul, and engaged in a subtle war of nerves. Their remarks that day resembled a ‘preliminary skirmish’ for the National Convention. (정 대표와 김 총리는 21일 오후 서울 여의도 국회 의원회관에서 열린 ‘6·3 지방선거 단체장 당선자 워크숍’에 나란히 참석해 신경전을 벌였다. 두 사람의 이날 발언은 전당대회 ‘전초전’을 방불케 했다.)

In his opening remarks, Representative Jung said, “Our goal is one, and it’s the same for everyone here: the success of the Yoon Suk Yeol administration, the re-creation of a conservative government, and making South Korea an unshakable advanced nation.” He added, “Going forward, the party, the government, and the presidential office will remain united as one team to complete the remaining livelihood and reform tasks.” He also sought to downplay rumors of conflict between the party and the presidential office, stating, “Through his European tour diplomacy, President Yoon Suk Yeol has stood tall as a world-class, global leader.” <<> In his subsequent congratulatory speech, Prime Minister Kim indirectly criticized the leadership of Jung Cheong-rae. <<> Prime Minister Kim said, “Although we achieved good results (in this election), regrettably, there are outcomes that make it somewhat difficult to declare a complete victory,” offering a different assessment of the local election results from that of the ‘Jung Cheong-rae leadership.’ He continued, “Now we have four years left; if the central government is shaken, if the president is shaken, what can we accomplish?” He added, “Above all, to transform into a Democratic Party that can give us the confidence to win this time, next time, and always, we must tighten our shoelaces again.” He also remarked, “Once I return to the party soon, I will do my utmost, however modestly.” Prime Minister Kim is expected to return to the party around the end of this month, when the appointment process for his successor, Prime Minister nominee Han Seong-sook, is finalized. <<> The Democratic Party is set to form a National Convention Preparatory Committee on the 26th. Following the precedent of President Yoon Suk Yeol, who resigned as party leader before forming the preparatory committee two years ago, Representative Jung may resign as leader around the Supreme Council meeting on or before the 24th. Within the party, it is widely accepted as a foregone conclusion that Representative Jung will seek a second term. <<> Another potential candidate for party leadership, Lawmaker Song Young-gil, also appeared on KBC Gwangju Broadcasting on the same day and took aim at Representative Jung. Song said, “Is the ruling party leader trying to pick a fight with the president? The ruling party should be a political group that acts as one body with the government to take responsibility for state affairs, but it’s deviating too much now, and I’m very concerned.” He added, “(Representative Jung) is trying to pursue his own political agenda.” There are possibilities for an alliance between Song and Prime Minister Kim. <<> At a press conference on the 19th regarding his European tour, President Yoon Suk Yeol targeted the heated National Convention of the Democratic Party, saying, “Don’t fight like mortal enemies” and “Can you achieve anything by waging war instead of competing?” However, it remains uncertain whether this will put a brake on the proceedings. <<> Former National Assembly Speaker Woo Won-shik declared on the same day that he would not run for party leader, saying, “If we hold a national convention that wounds each other, mocks opponents, finds faults, and fuels division, what will remain of the party afterward?” <<> By Koh Han-sol, Reporter sol@hani.co.kr (정 대표는 인사말에서 “우리의 목표는 하나이고, 여기 계신 모든 분이 똑같다. 이재명 정부 성공과 정권 재창출, 대한민국을 아무도 흔들 수 없는 선진 강국으로 만드는 것”이라며 “앞으로도 당·정·청이 원팀으로 똘똘 뭉쳐 남은 민생·개혁 과제들을 완수해가겠다”고 했다. 또 “유럽 순방 외교를 통해 이재명 대통령은 월드클래스, 세계적인 지도자로 우뚝 섰다”며 당청 ‘갈등설’ 무마에 나섰다.)

item.title: Year 2 of presidency: 'Half of senior secretaries replaced' for renewal...Third consecutive prosecutor-turned civil affairs secretary (집권 2년차 ‘수석 절반 교체’ 쇄신...‘3연속’ 검사 출신 민정수석)
item.description:
President Lee Jae-myung’s reshuffle of senior secretaries on the 21st, marking his second year in office, emphasized speed and renewal. The appointments are seen as an effort to stabilize the uneasy atmosphere following local elections and focus on communication and the implementation of national agenda tasks. <<> Chief of Staff Kang Hoon-sik explained the second-term overhaul of senior Cheong Wa Dae aides, stating, “It also reflects our determination to reform more and not slack off in self-discipline.” <<> Through the reshuffle, Cheong Wa Dae replaced five out of eleven senior-level positions (seven senior secretaries, one advisor, and three deputy chiefs), roughly half the total. Chief Kang said, “The AI Future Planning Secretary position, left vacant after former Senior Secretary Ha Jung-woo ran in the June 3 local elections, will be filled, so a total of six people are being replaced. It’s accurate to see this as a medium-to-large-scale Cheong Wa Dae personnel reshuffle.” Amid President Lee’s approval rating falling below 60% after the local elections, this move signals an intent to change the atmosphere by revamping the presidential office staff. <<> Notably, the replacements of the civil affairs secretary and social secretary stand out. <<> Following former Civil Affairs Secretaries Oh Kwang-soo and Bong Uk, President Lee has again selected a prosecutor-turned civil affairs secretary. Han Chan-sik, the new civil affairs secretary, served as head of the Eastern District Prosecutors’ Office from 2018 to 2019, leading investigations into the Moon Jae-in administration’s “Environment Ministry blacklist.” He left the prosecution in July 2019 when his junior at the Judicial Research and Training Institute, former President Yoon Suk Yeol, was appointed Prosecutor General. Secretary Han will oversee the establishment and stabilization of the Prosecution Service and the Serious Crimes Investigation Office, set to launch in October, as well as follow-up tasks such as revising the Criminal Procedure Act regarding supplementary investigation rights. Cheong Wa Dae reportedly hopes that Secretary Han, with his high level of understanding of the prosecution organization and investigation system, will quickly resolve these issues through a mediating role. <<> The Jo Kuk Innovation Party commented on Secretary Han’s record of investigating the Environment Ministry blacklist, saying, “With the second phase of prosecution reform discussions looming in the second half of this year, Secretary Han’s anti-reform past is concerning.” Resistance is also detectable among the ruling party’s hardline supporters, who demand prosecution reform. <<> The appointment of Kim Kyung-ja, a pharmacist-turned labor activist, as social secretary is also aimed at achieving swift state management. Secretary Kim has served as head of the Gyeonggi regional branch of the Health and Medical Workers’ Union and as vice chairperson and senior vice chairperson of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU). Secretary Kim has maintained a relationship with President Lee for over 20 years, having worked together on a civic movement to establish Seongnam City Hospital in 2003. Cheong Wa Dae expects Secretary Kim to play an active role in reforming labor policies, including industrial accident prevention. With Kim’s appointment, key government labor policy lines now feature multiple figures from labor circles. Labor Minister Kim Young-hoon is from the KCTU, and Cheong Wa Dae Labor Secretary Lee Ok-nam is from the Federation of Korean Trade Unions. <<> Additionally, Cheong Wa Dae appointed Seong Ki-hong, a veteran journalist with 30 years of experience, as communications secretary, signaling an intention to expand communication. Chief Kang stated, “We agreed that more active communication capabilities are needed.” <<> Changes were also made in the National Security Office. The newly appointed First Deputy Director of the National Security Office, Kang Geon-jak, served as head of the National Crisis Management Center and defense reform secretary under the Moon Jae-in administration, participating in the transition of wartime operational control (OPCON). This has led to interpretations that President Lee may be speeding up the early recovery of OPCON. Third Deputy Director Song Ki-ho was promoted internally, having moved from the inaugural post of director of the National Situation Room to economic security secretary last July. The “economic line” was excluded from this staff reshuffle. <<> President Lee is expected to announce a cabinet reshuffle early next month, following the confirmation hearing for Prime Minister nominee Han Sung-sook scheduled for the 25th-26th. Ministries mentioned as targets for the reshuffle include the Ministry of SMEs and Startups—left vacant by Han’s nomination—along with the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, and the Ministry of Health and Welfare. Justice Minister Jung Sung-ho is also rumored to possibly step down, as he has expressed a strong desire to return to the party. <<> Reporters: Seo Young-ji yj@hani.co.kr and Im Chul-hwi hwi@hani.co.kr (이재명 대통령이 21일 집권 2년차를 맞아 단행한 수석비서관 인사에서 속도와 쇄신에 방점을 찍었다. 지방선거 이후 어수선한 분위기를 다잡고, 소통과 국정 과제 이행에 중점을 두겠다는 인사로 풀이된다.)
